more_info.overview: Potassium sorbate is a potassium salt of sorbic acid, specified as a distinct chemical preparation for food manufacture. Its preservative role is to limit spoilage caused by microorganisms and extend the storage life of the food. The specified material is supplied as white powder or crystalline material.
more_info.daily_intake: 0-25 mg/kg body weight (JECFA, 1973). This is a combined sorbic-acid and sorbate limit, expressed as sorbic acid.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; fruit juices as defined by Directive 2001/112/EC and vegetable juices; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; unripened cheese excluding products falling in category 16.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
